lead: A fixed headlamp points where the car points. When the road bends, the beam keeps straight and the inside of the corner stays dark. An adaptive front lighting system (AFS) moves the lamp instead: a swivel motor turns it left and right with the steering, and a level motor tilts it up and down so the beam stays on the road when the boot is loaded. Sensors feed an ECU, and the ECU commands two small motors. Only a few universities teach this topic.
prereq: You need: the lamp and beam ideas from Chapter 2.5 and Chapter 2.6, and steering angle sensing from Unit 3.

blocks.text: A fixed headlamp is aimed once at the factory and bolted. An adaptive front lighting system (AFS) moves the lamp while you drive, in two independent motions.
Swivel is rotation about a vertical axis, called yaw. The lamp turns left or right with the steering wheel, so the beam enters the bend instead of lighting the hedge.

Levelling is rotation about a horizontal axis, called pitch. The lamp tips up or down so the cut-off line stays on the road. Load causes the problem: passengers in the back and a full boot lift the nose, and a fixed beam climbs into oncoming eyes. Braking dive and acceleration squat do the same briefly.

The two motions are separate. A car may have levelling alone, common with high-intensity discharge lamps because a bright arc must not glare. Swivel needs a steering angle sensor and speed. Most premium cars have both; some have swivel only.

Four inputs feed the AFS electronic control unit (ECU). The steering angle sensor reports steering wheel angle and rate. Wheel speed sensors report vehicle speed over the CAN bus. Ride height sensors link body to axle at front and rear; their difference gives pitch. A forward camera sees oncoming and leading vehicles.

The ECU computes target swivel and pitch angles, then commands two motors. A stepper motor moves in fixed steps and the ECU counts them; a DC motor uses a position sensor, often a potentiometer, to close the loop. The ECU compares commanded and measured angle and corrects.

Swivel is capped near 15°. A larger angle would send the beam across the centre line into oncoming traffic, so the command saturates. Speed shapes the command: a large angle at walking pace, a small one on the highway. On a fault the lamp parks at centre and dips, so the driver still has a low beam.

A matrix headlamp replaces the single source with many switchable LED segments. The camera locates a vehicle, the ECU blanks the segments aimed at it, and the rest stay on high beam. Adaptive driving beam is the function; matrix LED is one way to build it.

examples.question: A boot load sinks the rear of the car by 20 mm (the mass itself is not needed). The wheelbase (rear axle to front axle) is 2.0 m. Find the pitch angle and the levelling correction. The steering wheel is turned 90°, and the swivel command is 0.15 × steering wheel angle, capped at 15°. Find the swivel angle.
steps: The rear sinks, so the beam axis tilts up by 0.57°; the level motor must tilt it down by 0.57°.
Swivel command = 0.15 × 90° = 13.5°. This is below the 15° cap, so the lamp turns 13.5°.
examples.check:
import math

drop = 20/1000
theta = math.degrees(math.atan(drop/2.0))
print(round(theta, 2))
print(min(90*0.15, 15.0))

traps: Levelling corrects pitch (up-down) for load; swivelling corrects yaw (left-right) for steering. A car can have one without the other.
Check which angle the gain is defined on: here it is the steering wheel angle; if the gain is given on road wheel angle, divide by the steering ratio first.
Levelling direction: a sinking rear raises the beam, so the motor tilts the lamp down, not up.
Ignoring the swivel cap: at about 15° the command saturates, so more steering gives no more swivel.
Matrix LED is not a brighter lamp: segments switch off, so light on the road can fall.

quiz.q: Name two inputs to the AFS ECU.
quiz.a: Steering angle sensor and vehicle speed; also ride height and camera.

quiz.q: Why is swivel limited to about 15°?
quiz.a: Beyond it the beam crosses the centre line and glares oncoming drivers.

quiz.q: State the difference between AFS swivel and adaptive driving beam.
quiz.a: Swivel turns the whole beam; ADB blanks parts of a high beam around other vehicles.

quiz.q: Steering wheel 60°, ratio 15:1, gain 0.15 on steering wheel angle, cap 15°. Find road wheel angle and swivel.
quiz.a: Road wheel angle = 60/15 = 4°; swivel = 0.15 × 60 = 9°, below the 15° cap.

quiz.q: A 30 mm rear drop, wheelbase 2.5 m. Find the pitch angle.
The camera fails on a matrix-LED car. What should the AFS do, and why?
quiz.a: Drop to a fixed low beam and park the swivel at centre, because without detection the ECU cannot guarantee no glare.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production AFS now shares its camera with lane-keeping and automatic emergency braking, so the lamp function sits on a domain controller rather than a separate box. Pixel headlamps using micro-mirrors or LCD masks are in research; the aim is to draw a dark box around each road user while keeping high beam elsewhere. Search terms: adaptive driving beam regulation, matrix LED glare, AFS swivel actuator.
